Hi Marissa / Rachel,

Thanks for the demo today — Aurora Tech is excited about Redwood's latency/cost profile. Before we move to procurement, our legal team had a few clarifying questions on the DPA you shared. I've attached our redline for reference (Aurora_Tech_DPA_Redline.pdf). High-level items: 

- Controller vs. processor: Our legal team wants explicit language that Aurora is the controller and Redwood is the processor, with the processor only processing per documented instructions.
- Subprocessors: Please confirm the full list of subprocessors and whether Aurora can approve or object to any. 
- Breach notice: We need confirmation of notification timing (48 vs 72 hours) and the scope of info Redwood will provide.
- PII & data retention: Clarify how Redwood defines PII in the contract and the default data retention windows for logs, KV cache, and complete request/response records. Are retention windows configurable per customer?
- Data residency: Can we restrict processing to US-only regions for our account?

Can we get short, written answers to the above so I can share with our procurement/legal? Also propose a 30-minute follow-up call next week with your legal/security to go through items that need contract language tweaks. Availability: Tues/Wed mornings PST.

Thanks,
Samir

Hi Samir — thanks for sending the redline and for the candid list. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Controller/processor: Redwood’s default position is that customers (Aurora) are the controller and Redwood is the processor. We'll route the specific language in your redline to legal and confirm the exact wording.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessors list; we can provide the current list and an export. Our standard contract gives customers notice and the ability to object (narrow scope), but we can discuss approval/objection mechanics.
- Breach notice: I’ve looped in Dev (legal) and Neha (security) to confirm timing and content commitments.
- Retention & PII: High level — request/response logs and full request bodies are retained per account settings; default is 90 days for detailed logs, 365 days for aggregated telemetry. We do offer configurable retention and can discuss shorter retention or on-prem/private deployment for stricter requirements.
- Data residency: We support region pinning for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted accounts can be restricted to US regions on request (requires account config).

Next steps: Dev and Neha will reply with legal/security specifics and our subprocessors export. Would Tues 24 Feb 9:30am PST work for a 30-min call with our legal/security to review? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include procurement contacts.

Attaching Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf for your reference.

Hi Samir — looping in Neha for the security specifics; happy to answer the legal items below. Short answers (legal):

1) Controller/Processor: We confirm Redwood operates as a Processor for customer data processed via the Redwood platform. We process strictly on documented instructions from the controller (Aurora). We are open to adopting your redline language where it aligns with our standard processor obligations.

2) Subprocessors: The current authorized subprocessors list is published here: https://redwood-inference.com/subprocessors-list and I’ve attached a CSV export (redwood_subprocessors_2026-02.csv). We provide 30 days' notice of new subprocessors and an objection process which is narrowly tailored (we can discuss specifics).

3) Breach Notice: Our security incident response policy commits to providing an initial notification within 48 hours of confirming a security incident that affects customer data, with follow-ups as material facts are developed. For incidents that do not meet confirmed breach criteria we still notify customers per contract thresholds.

4) PII definition & retention: We treat any information that reasonably identifies an individual as PII. Defaults: request/response payload retention 90 days (hosted), KV cache retention depends on config (default 30 days for temporary cache), operational logs 90 days, and audit logs 365 days. We offer configurable retention and enterprise options (Dedicated/Private) for customers requiring shorter retention or on-prem processing.

5) Data residency: For hosted customers we can restrict processing to US regions; Dedicated and Private deployments give complete residency control. Note: certain features (model hosting, managed updates) have dependencies that may require specific region options — we can map this for Aurora’s required features.

If helpful, Neha can provide a short security bulletin that outlines encryption in transit/at rest, key management options (KMS/HSM), access controls, and SOC 2 availability. Let me know any contract clauses in your redline that we should prioritize.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_2026-02.csv (CSV, 12 KB)
